title: Fort Dearborn's officers' quarters get their upper piazza
items: The log officers' quarters on the fort's west side now have a covered walk along their parade front at second-floor height, on open posts with a railing. Gurdon Hubbard, recalling the fort as he saw it in 1818, describes this piazza running along the whole front at the level of the upper floor, reached by stairs outside. The building itself is unchanged.

It is marked as a reconstruction. Hubbard puts that building outside the stockade, but in the same book he puts the log officers' quarters inside it on the west, and nothing confirms that his 1818 building is the one standing in 1835. The walk's measurements are borrowed from the first fort's galleries, and the outside stairs are left out because nobody says where they ran.
